subject: Temporary slot bridge for model-sweep: reserved lane & policy waiver
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary slot bridge for model-sweep: reserved lane & policy waiver

Team —

Quick ask: Acme AI wants to run a multi-night scoring sweep (prod-like models) as part of their final evaluation before commit. The run is scheduled for Sept 20–24 during our US-west night window. Their tests are latency-sensitive and repeatable (same prompts each night). They are asking for a temporary reserved lane to guarantee no preemption during the nightly jobs and an autoscale policy waiver so the scheduler won't evict these slices mid-run.

What I need from infra/product/ops:
- Can we hold a short-term reservation (targeting ~12 GPU equivalents, see attached traffic_profile.json for token/sec distribution)?
- Can we carve an exemption window each night (02:00–06:00 PT) so the dedicated pool will not preempt these slices during the sweep?
- Ops: please draft a minimal runbook (start/stop, rollback, fallback model variant) and confirm monitoring hooks.

Why this matters: this is the last gating step for a mid-market POC that is likely to convert to a pilot reservation. We want to avoid a noisy test that fails due to preemption. I recognize this is an exception to our normal reservation policy — proposing limited duration and strict hours.

Attachments: acme_eval_schedule.csv, traffic_profile.json

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary slot bridge for model-sweep: reserved lane & policy waiver

Diego —

Thanks for the context. A couple quick questions so we can size this correctly:
1) Sustained RPS/peak tokens per sec during the 02:00–06:00 window? Your traffic_profile hinted at spikes but I need a 95th percentile figure to pick kernels and node counts.
2) Is this strictly inference (no training or large attention-sweeps)? If the jobs touch KV-cache warm starts we should plan memory sizing differently.
3) Fallback: if the dedicated pool can't honor the reservation because of capacity constraints, are we OK with a pre-agreed degraded SLO (e.g., quantized model variant with ~10–15% latency improvement but small quality delta)? Alternatively we can route to a different region (latency penalty) or to preemptible nodes during non-critical hours.

Operationally, I can provision up to 12 GPU-equivalent units without a long lead time (3 nodes of our standard 4-GPU slice) for a week if product signs off. Anything above that will require procurement lead + chargeback approval.

Can you push the 95th p95 numbers and the final business ask? I can then open INF-9812 and manual carve the lane for Sept 19 (preflight).

—Marcus
Sr. Infra Engineer
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary slot bridge for model-sweep: reserved lane & policy waiver

Diego / Marcus —

Product is aligned to support a short-term exception here given the commercial upside. A few constraints/asks from product/security:
- Limit reservation to 12 GPU-equivalents (no higher) for Sept 20–24, nightly 02:00–06:00 PT. We will not approve open-ended requests.
- Label the reservation in the Console as "acme-eval-EVAL-1423" so we can track cost/crediting back to the opportunity.
- Require a fallback model variant: please prepare a quantized v2 (8-bit) build that runs in <85% of the baseline GPU memory so we can auto-failover if infra signals capacity pressure. Marcus — can ops/prod coordinate a canary test on Sept 19?
- Finance note: Monica, this will be charged as short-term dedicated usage under the EVAL credit line. We need a quick approval for a one-week exception to our reservation-minimums.

I attached a one-page runbook template (runbook_draft.md) — fill in the gaps and ping me once INF-9812 is open.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Management
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, Ashley Nguyen <ashley@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary slot bridge for model-sweep: reserved lane & policy waiver

Thanks all — quick summary of agreed plan so Ops/prod/finance have the same expectations:
- Reservation: 12 GPU-equivalents (3 standard nodes) labeled "acme-eval-EVAL-1423".
- Window: nightly Sept 20–24, 02:00–06:00 PT. Preflight on Sept 19 at 02:00 for 30 minutes.
- Autoscale waiver: During the 02:00–06:00 window the nominated slices will not be eligible for preemption; non-critical background jobs must be scaled out of these nodes.
- Fallback: quantify v2 (8-bit) is the agreed degraded SLO variant. If infra signals >80% contention outside the reserved window we will switch to the quantized variant automatically.
- Runbook: laura_bennett to own runbook updates (attached draft). Marcus to create INF-9812 and prepare the carve. Monica to confirm quick finance approval.

Ashley — please confirm these windows are acceptable on your end and that your team will run the nightly sweep per the attached schedule.

Diego
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Ashley Nguyen <ashley@acme.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary slot bridge for model-sweep: reserved lane & policy waiver

Diego / team —

Confirmed on our side. Sept 20–24, nightly 02:00–06:00 PT works. We'll be running the canonical evaluation suite and will keep engineering on standby during the first night. If you need any additional telemetry (traces or request logs) from our side, send a pointer and we will enable it.

Thanks for moving quickly — Ashley Nguyen, Head of ML Eng, Acme AI
